source.title: Bleeding Pathways: Vanishing Discriminability in LLM Hidden States Fuels Jailbreak Attacks
source.authors: Ying-Jie Zhang; Tong Liu; Zhe Zhao; Guozhu Meng; Kai Chen

record.file_problem: Some figure text and layout are garbled, but the relevant prose and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates Refusal direction ablation (RFA), an attack attributed to the original refusal-direction work, and reports jailbreak success rates. It does not report the direction-extraction or ablation implementation details.
record.gate_note: The paper also measures benign-versus-harmful hidden-state separability and evaluates other attacks and defenses. Those results do not directly test the refusal-direction claim; the separability findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper runs Arditi et al.'s refusal direction ablation (RFA) as an attack on undefended models, including new ones (Qwen2.5, Phi-4, Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3-70B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill). It reports HarmBench-judged attack success rate (ASR), a result on whether ablating the direction removes refusal (V1). It also runs RFA on models after differently designed safety training (DeepAlign, Circuit Breaker, CAT), which bears on V7. The ablation implementation is not described and the measure differs from the original's refusal/safety scores, so this is T3, not T1. RFA is the ablation itself, not a jailbreak shown to suppress the direction, so V3 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that benign/harmful hidden-state separability decays during generation and that DeepAlign maintains it, cutting ASR of nine attacks to near zero with under 1% utility loss. They add that refusal-only training is fragile to direction removal (Sec. III-C, V-H), while diverse safe responses make single-direction manipulations less effective. They note RFA finds no valid direction in poorly aligned Mistral, the reasoning model and the uncensored model.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates the cited RFA attack and reports jailbreak success rates, but does not specify the direction extraction or projection procedure. It does not report the original study's full causal ablation/addition and capability evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: RFA's applicability differs by model: the authors say it cannot find a feasible refusal direction for Mistral, the reasoning model, and the unaligned Llama-3-8B-Lexi-Uncensored.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear-probe separability of benign vs harmful hidden states falls during generation: below 75% for Llama-3 under GCG, below 60% for DeepSeek-R1-Distill under CodeAttack. It is higher after DeepAlign.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmfulness separability of hidden states decays over response tokens in aligned chat and reasoning models.

fits_no_version.finding: SCAV-style probe on the last prompt token of Llama-3-8B: near-perfect for explicit queries, about 80% for DRA/CodeAttack-disguised queries (Appendix F, Fig. 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak disguises reduce input-level harmfulness separability at the last prompt token.

record.problems: RFA implementation details are not stated. The paper explicitly notes that RFA fails to find a feasible direction for some models, so zero ASR there does not establish that a valid direction ablation was performed. The study does not report uncertainty estimates for the RFA rates and does not test the original direction's addition or its effects on capabilities.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for RFA entries shown as N/A. Other attack results and utility measures were excluded because they do not apply the refusal-direction ablation or directly measure its attack effect.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; general abilities of ablated models; how the direction is extracted and selected.
No weight-edit or abliteration release test.
No test that other jailbreaks work by suppressing the direction; no training against ablation (DeepAlign is not RFA-specific).
No separation of harm judgment from refusal. The probes measure harm separability only.
Only one distilled reasoning model; no causal intervention on reasoning tokens.

missing.what: RFA ASR under different DeepAlign layer ranges and k values. Examples: Llama-3 layers 21-32 give 14.6% and 8-30 give 18.4%; Phi-4 26-40 gives 25.0% and 26-39 gives 8.4%; Llama-3 k=2 gives 7.4%. Whether the removable direction survives depends on training choices.
RFA ASR 0% for DeepAlign models trained on other models' data or without WildGuard filtering
No Attack ASR baselines for the Table I models (Llama-3 1.2%, Llama-2 0.2%, Mistral 35.6%, Qwen 0%, Phi-4 0%). Rows wrongly say 'not stated'.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a defense paper; RFA is one of the attacks used to evaluate it. RFA is attributed to Arditi et al. but its extraction, layer and position selection are never described, so 'fails to find a direction' may reflect the selection pipeline rather than the model. ASR is judged by the HarmBench classifier, not refusal-string matching. DeepAlign models give safe non-refusal answers, so low ASR there does not mean refusal was restored. The reader's V3 links were wrong: RFA is the ablation itself, and no defense was trained against it.

versions.untested_parts: No test of a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction, its removal across layers and positions, its addition, or the effect of those interventions on general abilities.
The study evaluates RFA attack success, but does not report training specifically against the refusal-direction ablation.
No geometric analysis distinguishing a single direction from an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
No experiment separating harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No transfer test of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No experiment varying when or how refusal is trained to test whether one removable direction exists.

The paper probes harmful-versus-benign hidden-state separability in a reasoning model and reports that RFA cannot find a refusal direction there, but does not test the causal refusal-direction intervention from V1.

source_check.notes: The RFA implementation is not stated: extraction layer, prompts, and whether the direction is re-extracted on defended models are all missing.
